title: Unit – 1 : Session – 1 : SLO – 2  |  Types of computers
sections: 2. c — High throughput and multi-user support
3. b — Built into another device for a specific task

1. A minicomputer is a mid-range, multi-user computer smaller than a mainframe but more powerful than a microcomputer; it supports several terminals at once. Real-time application: process control in a factory / college server.

2. General-purpose vs special-purpose: (i) General-purpose computers run many different applications (PCs); special-purpose computers are designed for one dedicated task. (ii) General-purpose machines are flexible but less optimized; special-purpose machines are faster/cheaper for their single task but not reprogrammable for other work.
Recommended: a Mainframe-class server (a high-end minicomputer is the budget alternative).

Justification: The university needs simultaneous access by many users (student records, exam processing, library). Mainframes are built exactly for this: very high throughput, strong multi-user support, large memory and I/O capacity, high reliability/availability, and transaction processing at scale. A minicomputer could serve a smaller load, but for a mid-sized university with concurrent access across departments, a mainframe's multi-user capability and reliability make it the most suitable choice.
Mainframe — large multi-user transaction servers (e.g., bank/airline reservation systems)
(Smartwatches — a) — are examples of embedded/microcomputer systems.)
5 devices with embedded computers: smartphone, washing machine, microwave oven, smart TV, car (ECU).

Example — washing machine: its embedded controller runs a fixed control program; it reads sensors (water level, load, temperature), times each wash/rinse/spin stage, and drives the motor and valves automatically. It is special-purpose: it does only washing control, reliably and cheaply.
